source_title: Care of adults with neurofibromatosis type 1: a clinical practice resource of the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG)
claim_text: In the Finnish registry cohort of NF1 patients there was no excess of leukemia or lymphoma, including juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia.
notes: Full text from locally supplied PDF (Genet Med 2018;20:671-682; not in PMC). Statement made by the ACMG adult NF1 practice resource citing ref 14 Uusitalo 2016 PMID 26926675. Secondary citation: not independent of the cited primary work; primary paper should be read for strength grading. Finnish registry analysis (ref 14, n=1,404 clinically diagnosed NF1, 19,076 person-years). The Gutmann 2017 Primer states that children with NF1 are predisposed to JMML; the two are recorded separately. The guideline cites genetic evidence (ref 51 Shannon 1994, loss of the normal NF1 allele in bone marrow) for the association.
independence_flags: secondary citation via guideline PMID 30006586 of ref 14
